BURHAN:v3p194/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p194/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p194/r8.claim: This rhetorical question suppresses its comparison: is the one whose heart is expanded like the person whose heart hardened and remains in disbelief?
BURHAN:v3p194/r8.anchor: وقوله ﴿ أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام ﴾ 5 أي كمن قسا قلبه ترك على ظلمه وكفره

BINTSHATI:v1p59/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p59/r1.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v1p59/r1.claim: Al-Raghib connects this verse with Moses' prayer and the description of one whose breast God expands for Islam, concluding that expansion is divine light, calm, and spirit.
BINTSHATI:v1p59/r1.anchor: شرح الصدر بسطه بنور إلهي وسكينة من جهة الله وروح منه

BINTSHATI:v1p59/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p59/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p59/r2.claim: The cited verses concern Moses' mission and believers opened to Islam's light, so they support a spiritual sense rather than cutting open and cleansing a physical heart.
BINTSHATI:v1p59/r2.anchor: ولا مجال لقول بشق الصدر وانتزاع القلب ثم غسله وتطهيره

BINTSHATI:v1p59/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p59/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p59/r4.claim: The five Meccan passages associate expansion with light and ease and contrast it with hardness, error, constriction, and disbelief, reinforcing a spiritual reading.
BINTSHATI:v1p59/r4.anchor: والآيات الخمس مكية. والشرح فيها جميعاً للصدر

BINTSHATI:v1p60/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p60/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p60/r1.claim: Across Qur'anic examples, expanding the breast means faith, truth's light, certainty, and peace, not a physical operation.
BINTSHATI:v1p60/r1.anchor: وهذا التتبع، يزيدنا بعداً عن المعنى المادي لشرح الصجر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r7.claim: Only people with living hearts accept the Qur'an; hardened hearts reject it and face the fate of earlier nations destroyed for rejecting messengers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p521/r7.anchor: only those people will profess faith in this Qur’ān whose nature is alive

ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r8.claim: An opened breast means submission to God; the Lord's light guides the seeker and is marked by removing blameworthy traits and acquiring noble sacred character.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p38/r8.anchor: للإنقياد إليه سبحانه ( فهو على نور من ربه ) يستضيء به في طلبه سبحانه ومن علامات هذا النور

RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r1.claim: After establishing proofs for obedience and turning away from worldly life, Rāzī says their benefit is complete only when God opens the chest and illuminates the heart.
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r1.anchor: لما بالغ في تقرير البيانات الدالة على وجوب الإقبال على طاعة الله تعالى ووجوب الإعراض عن الدنيا بين بعد ذلك أن الانتفاع بهذه البيانات لا يكمل إلا إذا شرح الله الصدور ونور القلوب

RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r2.claim: Rāzī refers readers to his fuller discussion of chest expansion and guidance under 6:125, while briefly restating it here.
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r2.anchor: واعلم أنا بالغنا في سورة الأنعام

RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r3.claim: Human souls differ essentially: some are noble, luminous, and drawn to spiritual realities, while others are base, turbid, and drawn to bodily life; observation confirms this variation.

RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r4.claim: Chest expansion is an innate strong readiness in the soul; when it exists, a slight cause brings it into action, like sulfur ignited by a small flame.
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r4.anchor: المراد بشرح الصدر هو ذلك الاستعداد الشديد الموجود في فطرة النفس

RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r5.claim: The “light” is guidance and knowledge; chest readiness comes first, and its absence leaves a person unable to benefit from proofs, which may instead deepen aversion.
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r5.anchor: وأما النور فهو عبارة عن الهداية والمعرفة

RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r6.claim: When a soul is remote from spiritual states and absorbed in bodily desires, repeated proofs lessen its hardness and darkness; these principles are needed to understand the verses.
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r6.anchor: كلما كان إيراد الدلائل اليقينية والبراهين الباهرة

RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r7.claim: Rāzī says the arguments of his school on determinism and predestination, and the opponents’ responses, were already discussed under 6:125.
RAZI-FULL:v26p231/r7.anchor: أما استدلال أصحابنا في مسألة الجبر والقدر وكلام الخصوم عليه فقد تقدم هناك

RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r1.claim: The predicate after man is omitted, as in 39:9: the opened and guided person is compared with one whose heart is sealed and who is unguided; the following woe supplies the answer.
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r1.anchor: من محذوف الخبر كما في قوله

RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r2.claim: Because remembrance ordinarily brings light, guidance, and reassurance, Rāzī asks why this verse associates it with hard hearts; he cites 13:28.
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r2.anchor: أن ذكر الله سبب لحصول النور والهداية

RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r3.claim: For souls of evil, turbid nature that are far from spiritual things and inclined to bestial traits, hearing God’s remembrance can increase hardness and turbidity.
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r3.anchor: إن النفس إذا كانت خبيثة الجوهر

RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r4.claim: One agent can affect recipients differently: sunlight darkens a dyer’s face but whitens his cloth, and its heat softens wax while hardening salt; the same speech also pleases one listener and repels another.
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r4.anchor: كنور الشمس يسود وجه القصار ويبيض ثوبه

RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r5.claim: Rāzī reports that when 23:12–14 was recited, ʿUmar and another man both said “Blessed is God, the best of creators”; the Prophet told him to write it as revealed, after which ʿUmar’s faith grew and the other man’s disbelief grew. No grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r5.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r6.claim: Thus remembrance gives light and reassurance to pure spiritual souls but hardens evil satanic souls; when the chief spiritual medicine worsens an illness, that soul is beyond cure and at the worst degree of evil.
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r6.anchor: إذا عرفت هذا لم يبعد أيضا أن يكون ذكر الله

RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r7.claim: The following discussion describes the Qur’an as light, healing, guidance, and reassurance; its producing greater hardness for such a person shows the soul’s extreme vileness.
RAZI-FULL:v26p231#2/r7.anchor: ولما بين تعالى ذلك أردفه بما يدل على أن القرآن سبب لحصول النور والشفاء والهداية وزيادة الاطمئنان

STUDYQURAN:39:22/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r1.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r1.claim: An omitted comparison completes the opening: is the expanded person like one without faith, or like one whose heart is sealed?
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r1.anchor: “[is he] like he who is not” or “[is he] like one whose heart He has sealed” (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:39:22/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r2.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r2.claim: The breast is the locus of the heart and fountainhead of the spirit, and so the seat of inspirations, thoughts, and intentions.
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r2.anchor: the locus of the heart and the fountainhead of the spirit (Bḍ)

STUDYQURAN:39:22/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r3.claim: The Quran connects the breast with what God knows within people and with the disclosure of inner contents on Judgment Day.
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r3.anchor: The Quran mentions frequently that God knows what lies within breasts

STUDYQURAN:39:22/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r4.claim: Breast expansion is associated with belief, while contraction is associated with disbelief.
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r4.anchor: While the breast’s expansion is associated with belief

STUDYQURAN:39:22/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r5.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r5.claim: Following light from God means that God has opened the heart to spiritual knowledge, or maʿrifah, and guidance.
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r5.anchor: God has opened one’s heart to spiritual knowledge(maʿrifah ) and guidance (Bḍ)

STUDYQURAN:39:22/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r6.speaker: The Prophet
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r6.claim: The Prophet says light entering the heart makes it spacious; its sign is turning toward the eternal abode, shunning delusion, and preparing for death.
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r6.anchor: The Prophet: “When light enters the heart, it expands and it becomes spacious.”

STUDYQURAN:39:22/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r7.claim: Hardened hearts remain in dark desire and pursue worldly things, far from the lights of knowledge and guidance.
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r7.anchor: stew in the dark recesses of desire and seek the things of this world

STUDYQURAN:39:22/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r8.claim: Hearts become hardened, sealed, or covered through wrongdoing and loss of Divine Favor, making them unreceptive to revelation and remembrance; Moses even asks that Pharaoh’s people be hardened.
STUDYQURAN:39:22/r8.anchor: “hardened,” “sealed,” or “covered” as a result of their own wrongdoing and the consequent loss of Divine Favor

BURSEVI:v8p71/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p71/r1.claim: The hamza is interrogative and condemnatory, the fa links to an omitted clause, and man is either conditional or relative with an elided predicate indicated by what follows.
BURSEVI:v8p71/r1.anchor: للاستفهام الإنكاري ، والفاء : للعطف على محذوف

BURSEVI:v8p71/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p71/r2.claim: شرح originally means spreading or opening meat; opening the breast is by divine light, tranquility, and a spirit from God.
BURSEVI:v8p71/r2.anchor: ومنه شرح الصدر بنور إلهي وسكينة من جهته تعالى وروح منه

BURSEVI:v8p71/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71/r3.speaker: أبو السعود
BURSEVI:v8p71/r3.claim: Abu al-Su'ud defines expansion for Islam as completing one's readiness for it: the chest houses the heart, source of the spirit linked to the soul that accepts Islam, and its expansion widens and illumines the heart before Islam.
BURSEVI:v8p71/r3.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" : شرح الصدر للإسلام عبارة عن تكميل الاستعداد له

BURSEVI:v8p71/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p71/r4.claim: Bursevi frames the contrast as whether all people are equal, introducing the distinction between the one given an open breast and others.
BURSEVI:v8p71/r4.anchor: والمعنى : أكل الناس سواء فمن بالفارسية : (بس هركسى ويا آنكس كه).

BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r1.claim: God made the person broad-chested and ready for Islam; he remained on original human disposition without acquired distortions.
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r1.anchor: أي : خلقه متسع الصدر مستعدا للإسلام

BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r2.claim: The open-hearted person rests in great divine light: God's favor enables him to recognize and follow the truth in cosmic and revealed signs, unlike those who darken their hearts by choice and ignore them.
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r2.anchor: بموجب ذلك مستقر {على نور} عظيم {من ربه}

BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r3.claim: The contrast recalls the person whose breast God makes constricted and closed, as in 6:125; light and darkness, like knowledge and ignorance, are not equal.
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r3.anchor: يعني : ليس من هو على نور كمن هو على ظلمة

BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r4.claim: A Muslim's light and happiness depend on knowledge and gnosis; each believer's distinctive gnosis determines the degree of spiritual rank.
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r4.anchor: واعلم أنه لا نور ولا سعادة لمسلم إلا بالعلم والمعرفة

BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r5.claim: Faith and gnosis are lights of unequal reach: common believers resemble candlelight or a lamp, the truthful resemble moon and stars, and prophets the sun or more, revealing different expanses of the unseen realm.
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r5.anchor: فإيمان آحاد العوام نوره كنور الشمع وبعضهم نوره كنور السراج وإيمان الصديقين نوره كنور القمر والنجوم

BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r6.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r6.claim: A prophetic report says people will be brought out of Hell according to measures of faith from half or quarter of a grain down to an atom, showing that faith's grades and their lights differ at the Resurrection, especially on the Bridge.
BURSEVI:v8p71#2/r6.anchor: ولهذا جاء في الحديث : "إنه يقال يوم القيامة أخرجوا من النار

BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r2.claim: Hardness is a thickening of the heart, named by analogy with hard stone; muqāsāt is the process of bearing or treating hardship.
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r2.anchor: القسوة غلظ القلب وأصله من حجر قاس والمقاساة معالجة ذلك

BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r3.claim: من can indicate cause or explanation: because of God's remembrance, which should open breasts and reassure hearts, they recoil and harden further when God and His signs are recalled.
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r3.anchor: ومن أجلية وسببية كما في قوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r4.claim: Their worsening hardness is compared to the increase of impurity in 9:125.

BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r5.claim: A reading with عن instead of من means that their hearts are hardened against accepting God's remembrance.
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r5.anchor: وقرىء عن ذكر الله ؛ أي : فويل للذين غلظت قلوبهم

BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r6.speaker: مالك بن دينار
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r6.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says no punishment strikes a servant worse than a hardened heart, and God removes mercy from a people only when angry with them.
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r6.anchor: وعن مالك بن دينار رحمه الله ما ضرب عبد بعقوبة أعظم من قسوة قلبه

BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r7.speaker: الله
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r7.claim: In a private address to Moses, God warns that prolonged worldly hopes harden the heart, which then becomes distant from Him; Moses should wear worn clothes but keep a renewed heart.
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r7.anchor: وقال الله تعالى لموسى عليه السلام في مناجاته يا موسى : لا تطل في الدنيا أملك

BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r8.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r8.claim: A hadith identifies love of food, sleep, and ease as three causes of hardness in the heart.
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r8.anchor: وفي الحديث : "تورث القسوة في القلب ثلاث خصال

BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r9.speaker: عائشة الصديقة
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r9.claim: Al-Kashf al-Asrar says hardness grows from many sins and quotes Aisha that the first innovation after the Prophet was satiety; Dhun-Nun says a full meal brought him sin, while hunger let Shibli find fresh wisdom and lessons.
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r9.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" : (بدانكه ابن قسوة دل از بسيارى معصيت خيزد عائشة صديقه

BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r10.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r10.claim: A hadith praises prolonged hunger and reflection, condemns gluttony, drinking, and much sleep, and recommends eating and drinking to half-full as part of prophecy.
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r10.anchor: وفي الحديث : "أفضلكم عند الله أطولكم جوعا وتفكرا

BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r11.claim: Bursevi quotes Sa'di's poem advising moderate eating, likening the human stomach to a vessel for food and remembrance rather than an empty space for appetite alone.
BURSEVI:v8p71#3/r11.anchor: باندازه خورزاد اكر آدمى جنين برشكم آدمى يا خمى

BURSEVI:v8p72/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p72/r1.claim: Those far from God, whose hearts have hardened, are in manifest misguidance obvious even to a minimally perceptive observer.
BURSEVI:v8p72/r1.anchor: البعداء الموصوفون بما ذكر من قساوة القلب

BURSEVI:v8p72/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p72/r2.claim: The verse applies generally to anyone whose breast God opens by creating faith within.
BURSEVI:v8p72/r2.anchor: واعلم أن الآية عامة فيمن شرح صدره للإسلام بخلق الإيمان فيه

BURSEVI:v8p72/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p72/r3.claim: One view says the verse was revealed about Hamza and Ali, whose breasts were opened to Islam, and Abu Lahab and his son, whose hearts hardened.
BURSEVI:v8p72/r3.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في حمزة بن عبد المطلب وعلي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنهما وأبي لهب

BURSEVI:v8p72/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72/r4.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p72/r4.claim: In a report about the verse's revelation, the Prophet explains that divine light entering the heart expands it; its signs are turning to the eternal home, renouncing the delusive world, and preparing for death before it arrives.
BURSEVI:v8p72/r4.anchor: روي في الخبر أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية ، قالوا : كيف ذلك يا رسول الله

BURSEVI:v8p72/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72/r5.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p72/r5.claim: Faith is a light illuminating the heart's lamp and Islam its ray in the breast's niche; an expanded breast lives by the light of the Lord's care.
BURSEVI:v8p72/r5.anchor: يشير إلى أن الإيمان نور ينور الله به مصباح قلوب عباده المؤمنين والإسلام ضوء نور الإيمان

BURSEVI:v8p72/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p72/r6.claim: Signs of this light include erasing blameworthy worldly desires, cultivating love of the Hereafter, good deeds and noble character; God erases and confirms as He wills, as 13:39 says.
BURSEVI:v8p72/r6.anchor: ومن أمارات ذلك النور محو آثار ظلمات الصفات الذميمة النفسانية من حب الدنيا وزينتها وشهواتها

BURSEVI:v8p72/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p72/r7.claim: Another sign is that remembrance softens the heart and deepens longing for God, making the seeker weary of worldly trials and bestial, predatory, and satanic traits so that he flees to God.
BURSEVI:v8p72/r7.anchor: ومن أماراته أن تلين قلوبهم لذكر الله فتزداد أشواقهم إلى لقاء الله تعالى وجواره

BURSEVI:v8p72/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v8p72/r8.claim: The way proceeds through lights of knowledge, understanding, certainty, manifestation of the attributes, witnessing of the essence, and the majesty of divine oneness, until ordinary notions of self, aim, nearness, and separation fall away.
BURSEVI:v8p72/r8.anchor: نور المشاهدة بظهور الذات ثم أنوار جلال الصمدية بحقائق التوحيد

BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r1.speaker: جامي
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r1.claim: Jami's poem counsels the seeker not to dwell on nearness, distance, union, or separation after transcending such distinctions.
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r1.anchor: جامى مكن انديشه زنز ديكى ودورى لا قرب ولا بعد ولا وصل ولا بين

BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r2.speaker: الواسطي
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r2.claim: Al-Wasiti calls expansion's light a great gift borne only by those upheld with divine care: care protects bodily forms, while providence protects spiritual realities.
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي : نور الشرح منحة عظيمة

BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r3.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r3.claim: Al-Kashf al-Asrar maps four inner layers: breast as the seat of Islam's covenant, heart as faith's light, fu'ad as the secret of witnessing, and shighaf as the station of love, with Quranic parallels at 2:22, 53:11, and 12:30.
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r3.anchor: وفي "كشف الأسرار" : (بدان كه دل آدمى را جهارا برده است. برده أول صدر

BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r4.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r4.claim: God first clears the breast of whims and innovations and sets it on the Sunnah, then purifies the heart of worldly attachment and blameworthy traits, opens knowledge and wisdom in the fu'ad, and leads the shighaf from clay toward annihilation.
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r4.anchor: اول نظرى كند بصد روى تاسينه وى از هوى وبدعتها باك كردد وقدم وى برجاده سنت مستقيم شود

BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r5.claim: The author adopts a three-part account of light: the tongue's light is testimony to oneness, the body's is service and obedience, and the heart's is longing and love; they lead respectively to Paradise, Firdaws, and beholding the Beloved, with verses 5:85, 18:107, and 75:22-23 as proofs.
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r5.anchor: نور زبان توحيد است وشهادت. ونورتن خدمت است وطاعت.

BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r6.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r6.claim: A hadith warns that people blessed with divine favors have enemies and should beware of them.
BURSEVI:v8p72#2/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن لأهل النعم أعداء فاحذروهم"

TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r1.claim: The person whose heart God expands for Islam knows Him, affirms His oneness and lordship, submits to obedience, and gains insight and certainty through truth's illumination.
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r1.anchor: فهو على بصيرة مما هو عليه ويقين، بتنوير الحق في قلبه، فهو لذلك لأمر الله متبع

TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r2.claim: The comparison's other half and the interrogative's answer are left implicit for listeners to infer; the warning about hardened hearts supplies the contrast.
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r2.anchor: وجواب الاستفهام اجتزاء بمعرفة السامعين المراد من الكلام، إذ ذكر

TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r3.claim: Qatada identifies the light as God's Book, which the believer believes, takes, and follows.
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام

TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī explains that God has made the person's chest spacious for Islam.
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r4.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: {أفمن شرح الله صدره

TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the light as guidance.
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r5.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: {أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام}

TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r6.claim: Mujahid says the one whose breast is open to Islam is unlike the one whose heart is hardened.
TAB-FULL:v20p189#2/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد، {أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام}

TAB-FULL:v20p190/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p190/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p190/r1.claim: Hardened hearts are dry, distant from God's remembrance, and turned away from the Quran He sent as a reminder; their owners do not believe or affirm its contents.
TAB-FULL:v20p190/r1.anchor: كما يقال في الكلام: أتخمت من طعام أكلته، وعن طعام أكلته بمعنى واحد

TAB-FULL:v20p190/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p190/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p190/r2.claim: Here من means عن; Arabic can use either preposition in expressions such as being made ill from food one ate.
TAB-FULL:v20p190/r2.anchor: أتخمت من طعام أكلته، وعن طعام أكلته بمعنى واحد

TABATABAI:39:21-22/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r9.claim: After the preceding signs as reminders for people of understanding and God's guided, this verse explains why the guided differ from the misguided: they have light from God and hearts receptive to the best words.
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r9.anchor: لما ذكر في الآية السابقة أن فيما ذكره من إنزال الماء وإنبات النبات ذكرى لأولي الألباب وهم عباده المتقون

TABATABAI:39:21-22/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r10.claim: The predicate after أفمن شرح الله صدره is omitted and supplied by the contrast with those whose hearts are hard; the interrogative denies that the two are equal.
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r10.anchor: خبره محذوف يدل عليه قوله { فويل للقاسية قلوبهم } الخ أي كالقاسية قلوبهم

TABATABAI:39:21-22/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r11.claim: Expanding the breast for Islam means being able to receive the true word, which is submission to God's will, with discernment and insight rather than unexamined acceptance.
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r11.anchor: وشرح الصدر بسطه ليسع ما يلقى إليه من القول وإذ كان ذلك للإسلام وهو التسليم لله فيما أراد وليس إلا الحق

TABATABAI:39:21-22/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r12.claim: The person is pictured as riding a light, seeing truths enter the spacious breast and distinguishing them from falsehood; the misguided lack both the spacious breast and that light.
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r12.anchor: فجعله بحسب التمثيل راكب نور يسير عليه ويبصر ما يمر به في ساحة صدره الرحب الوسيع من الحق فيبصره ويميزه من الباطل

TABATABAI:39:21-22/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r13.claim: Hardness of heart entails lacking an expanded breast and light; such people do not take heed from God's signs and therefore fail to find guidance.
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r13.anchor: تفريع على الجملة السابقة بما يدل على أن القاسية القلوب

TABATABAI:39:21-22/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r14.claim: The verse defines guidance by its signs, an expanded breast and light from God, and defines misguidance by its sign, a heart hardened against God's remembrance.
TABATABAI:39:21-22/r14.anchor: وفي الآية تعريف الهداية بلازمها وهو شرح الصدر وجعله على نور من ربه

TABATABAI:39:36-37/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r10.claim: A report says that when divine light enters the heart it expands; its signs are detachment from worldly delusion, turning toward the eternal abode, and preparing for death before it arrives.
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r10.anchor: روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:39:36-37/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r11.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthūr transmits the report through Ibn Mardawayh from Ibn Masʿūd, al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī from Ibn ʿUmar, and Ibn Jarīr and others from Qatāda.
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r11.anchor: ورواه في الدر المنثور عن ابن مردويه عن عبد الله بن مسعود

TABATABAI:39:36-37/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r12.speaker: القمي
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r12.claim: Al-Qummī’s tafsir says this verse was revealed about ʿAlī; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī objects that the whole sūra’s one-time revelation does not fit that report.
TABATABAI:39:36-37/r12.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى

TABRISI:39:22/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22/r5.claim: The relative clause with man is the subject and its predicate is omitted, understood as is one whose chest God expanded like one whose heart hardened by abandoning remembrance?
TABRISI:39:22/r5.anchor: من مع صلته مبتدأ والخبر محذوف تقديره أفمن شرح الله صدره كمن قسا قلبه

TABRISI:39:22/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22/r6.claim: Alternatively, the phrase can refer to shrinking at the mention of God, with qasat min dhikr Allah understood as hardening when people mention God.
TABRISI:39:22/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تشمئز عند ذكر الله. فيقال: قست من ذكر الله

TABRISI:39:22/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22/r10.claim: God's opening of the breast means widening the heart to accept Islam and remain steadfast in it; the address is to the Prophet though it applies to all morally responsible people.
TABRISI:39:22/r10.anchor: يخاطب نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن كان المراد جميع المكلفين

TABRISI:39:22/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22/r11.claim: The first of three means by which the breast is opened is the strength of God's proofs, a benefit specific to scholars.
TABRISI:39:22/r11.anchor: وشرح الصدر يكون بثلاثة أشياء: أحدها: بقوة الأدلة التي نصبها الله تعالى

TABRISI:39:22/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22/r12.claim: The second means is God's graces, renewed for a person continually.
TABRISI:39:22/r12.anchor: والثاني: بالألطاف التي تتجدد له حالا بعد حال كما قال سبحانه

TABRISI:39:22-23/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22-23/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22-23/r1.claim: He quotes 47:17, where God increases the guidance of those already guided.

TABRISI:39:22-23/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22-23/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22-23/r2.claim: A third explanation is that guidance comes through reinforcing proofs, resolving doubts, and casting insights.
TABRISI:39:22-23/r2.anchor: والثالث: بتوكيد الأدلة وحل الشبهة وإلقاء الخواطر

TABRISI:39:22-23/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22-23/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22-23/r3.claim: Being on light means being upon a proof and guidance from one's Lord.
TABRISI:39:22-23/r3.anchor: { فهو على نور } أي على دلالة وهدى

TABRISI:39:22-23/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22-23/r4.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:39:22-23/r4.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says proofs are called light because they reveal truth as light reveals worldly things.
TABRISI:39:22-23/r4.anchor: شبه الأدلة بالنور لأن بها يعرف الحق كما بالنور تعرف أمور الدنيا عن الجبائي

TABRISI:39:22-23/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22-23/r5.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:39:22-23/r5.claim: Qatāda identifies the light as God's Book, which is the source one follows and returns to.
TABRISI:39:22-23/r5.anchor: وقيل: النور كتاب الله عز وجل فبه نأخذ وإليه ننتهي عن قتادة

TABRISI:39:22-23/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22-23/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22-23/r6.claim: The comparison with the hard-hearted person is omitted; the following warning identifies the missing counterpart.
TABRISI:39:22-23/r6.anchor: وحذف كمن هو قاسي القلب يدل على المحذوف

TABRISI:39:22-23/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22-23/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22-23/r7.claim: The hard-hearted are habituated to disbelief and stubbornly attached to it; preaching, inducement, threats, and Quran recitation do not soften them.
TABRISI:39:22-23/r7.anchor: وهم الذين ألفوا الكفر وتعصبوا له وتصلبت قلوبهم حتى لا ينجع فيها وعظ

TABRISI:39:22-23/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:22-23/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:22-23/r8.claim: Their manifest error means they have turned away from the truth in an obvious way.
TABRISI:39:22-23/r8.anchor: أي عدول عن الحق { مبين } أي ظاهر واضح

TABRISI:39:23-25/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:23-25/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:23-25/r14.claim: The chest-opening question follows the earlier proofs of divine unity and justice: reflection on them opens the heart and settles certainty.
TABRISI:39:23-25/r14.anchor: إنما اتصل قوله { أفمن شرح الله صدره }

THALABI:v8p229/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p229/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v8p229/r1.claim: Ibn Masud reports the Prophet explaining that the heart opens when light enters it.
THALABI:v8p229/r1.anchor:
عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال:
قال رسول الله (عليه السلام) : «أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه»

THALABI:v8p229/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p229/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
THALABI:v8p229/r2.claim: The Prophet gives the signs as turning toward the eternal home, withdrawing from the deceptive world, and preparing for death before it arrives.
THALABI:v8p229/r2.anchor: قال: «الإنابة إلى دار الخلود والتجافي عن دار الغرور والتأهب للموت قبل نزول الموت» » .

THALABI:v8p229/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p229/r3.speaker: الثمالي
THALABI:v8p229/r3.claim: Al-Thumali says the verse was revealed concerning Ammar ibn Yasir.
THALABI:v8p229/r3.anchor: وقال الثمالي: بلغنا أنها نزلت في عمار بن ياسر

THALABI:v8p229/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p229/r4.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v8p229/r4.claim: Muqatil identifies the person whose breast God opens as the Prophet Muhammad.
THALABI:v8p229/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام يعني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم.

THALABI:v8p229/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p229/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p229/r5.claim: The hardhearted are Abu Jahl and other disbelievers.
THALABI:v8p229/r5.anchor: فويل للقاسية قلوبهم من ذكر الله أبو جهل وذويه من الكفار

THALABI:v8p229/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p229/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
THALABI:v8p229/r6.claim: Abu Said reports a divine saying: seek needs from generous people, where God placed mercy, not hardhearted people, where He placed wrath.
THALABI:v8p229/r6.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: «قال الله عز وجل: اطلبوا الحوائج من السمحاء فاني جعلت فيهم رحمتي

THALABI:v8p229/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p229/r7.speaker: أبو الدرداء
THALABI:v8p229/r7.claim: Abu al-Darda reports that God loves gentleness and humble, patient, merciful hearts that teach good and call to obedience, and hates hard hearts that sleep without remembering Him.
THALABI:v8p229/r7.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «إن الله رفيق يحب الرفق في الأمر كله ويحب كل قلب خاشع حليم رحيم

THALABI:v8p230/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p230/r1.speaker: مالك بن دينار
THALABI:v8p230/r1.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says no punishment is greater than a hard heart, and God removes mercy from a people when angry with them.
THALABI:v8p230/r1.anchor: عن مالك بن دينار قال: ما ضرب عبد بعقوبة أعظم من قسوة قلبه وما غضب الله تعالى على قوم إلا نزع منهم الرحمة.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r3.claim: God's expanding a person's chest means making it spacious for Islam and guiding that person to the religion.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r3.anchor: وسعه { للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه } أي: فاهتدى إلى دين الإسلام

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r4.claim: The following warning about hardened hearts supplies the unstated comparison: the guided person is unlike one whose heart is sealed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:39:21-23/r4.anchor: كمن طبع على قلبه، ويدل على هذا المحذوف قوله: { فويل للقاسية قلوبهم من ذكر الله

QASHANI:39:22-24/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:22-24/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:22-24/r1.claim: At subsistence after annihilation, God's light purifies the heart with gifted divine existence, so the expanded breast holds Real and creation without veiling and sees detail within unity and unity within multiplicity; Islam is annihilation and surrender to God.
QASHANI:39:22-24/r1.anchor: بنوره حال البقاء بعد الفناء ونقى قلبه بالوجود الموهوب الحقاني فيسع صدره الحق والخلق من غير احتجاب بأحدهما عن الآخر فيشاهد التفصيل في عين الوحدة والتوحيد في عين الكثرة

QASHANI:39:22-24/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:22-24/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:22-24/r2.claim: The one on a light from his Lord sees his Lord.

QASHANI:39:22-24/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:39:22-24/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:39:22-24/r3.claim: Hard hearts refuse to receive God's remembrance because they cling to bodily pleasures and turn away from sacred perfections, straying clearly from the way of truth.
QASHANI:39:22-24/r3.anchor: للذين قست قلوبهم من قبول ذكر الله لشدة ميلها إلى اللذات البدنية وإعراضها عن الكمالات القدسية

ELMALILI:39:22-31/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:39:22-31/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:39:22-31/r1.claim: Elmalılı renders God’s opening a person’s breast to Islam as being on light from the Lord, and describes hearts hardened from God’s remembrance as hard.
ELMALILI:39:22-31/r1.anchor: Demek ki her kimin Allah bağrını İslâm’a açmış ise işte o Rabbinden bir nûr üzerinde değil mi? O hâlde vay o Allah’ın zikrinden kalbleri katılara!

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:21/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:21/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:21/r1.claim: The revival and drying of plants after rain illustrates God’s absolute sovereignty over the universe, then leads to the same divine power’s effect on human spiritual development.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:21/r1.anchor: Yağmur ve onun sayesinde yetişen bitki çeşitleriyle tabiatın canlanması, ardından bitkilerin kuruyup toza toprağa karışması örneğinden yola çıkılarak, ilâhî kudret ve iradenin evren üzerindeki mutlak hükümranlığına dikkat çekilmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:21/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:21/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:21/r2.claim: Just as God revives nature through rain, His guidance opens a person’s heart to Islam, gives the soul a posture of submission to divine commands, and illuminates it with His light.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:21/r2.anchor: Yağmurla tabiatı canlandıran irade, hidayetiyle de insanın gönlünü İslâm’a açmakta; ona, ilâhî buyruklara teslim olan bir ruh yapısı kazandırmakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:21/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:21/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:21/r3.claim: Hard-hearted people are those who give God no place in their hearts, show no lived trace of professed belief, fail to learn from warnings, and become insensitive to truth; their dulled moral discernment leaves them in manifest error.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:39:21/r3.anchor: gönüllerinde Allah’a yer vermeyen, –putperest Araplar’ın yaptığı gibi– sorulduğunda O’na inandıklarını söyleseler bile, hayatlarında bu inancın izi görülmeyen

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r2.claim: Those decreed punishment include people sentenced to the Fire and people sentenced to the punishment of being veiled from God today; they remain trapped behind their heart’s veil, even if they belong outwardly to the faithful.
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r2.anchor: فريق حقت عليهم كلمة بعذابهم في النار ، وفريق حقت عليهم كلمة العذاب بالحجاب اليوم

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r3.claim: God’s promises of Paradise to the obedient, forgiveness to the repentant, and presence and arrival to seekers are certain, provided seekers do not lapse into an intervening pause.
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r3.anchor: وعد المطيعين بالجنة - ولا محالة لا يخلف ، ووعد التائبين بالمغفرة - ولا محالة يغفر لهم

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r8.claim: The answer to the verse’s implied comparison is omitted: is the one whose breast God expands for Islam like the one whose breast is not expanded?
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r8.anchor: جواب هذا الخطاب محذوف . . . أي أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام كمن ليس كذلك

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r9.speaker: الرسول - صلى الله عيله وسلم -
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r9.claim: The Prophet explained the breast’s expansion as a light cast into the heart; its sign is turning away from the delusive world toward the eternal home and preparing for death before it arrives.
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r9.anchor: لما نزلت هذه الآية سئل الرسول - صلى الله عيله وسلم - عن الشرح المذكور فيها ، فقال : ( ذلك نور يقذف في القلب )

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r10.claim: The divine light unfolds through successive stations: signs of knowledge, clarity of understanding, added certainty, disclosure of attributes, witnessing of the Essence, and the realities of tawhid; beyond these, ordinary categories of presence and absence or nearness and distance fall away.
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r10.anchor: ثم نور المكاشفة بتجلي الصفات ، ثم نور المشاهدة بظهور الذات ، ثم أنوار الصمدية بحقائق التوحيد

QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r11.claim: Hard hearts are those not struck by intimations of recognition, remaining in denial, enduring error, and lasting ignorance.
QUSHAYRI:v3p116/r11.anchor: اي الصلبة قلوبهم ، لم تقرعها خواطر التعريف فبقيت على نكرة الجحد

BURHAN:v4p419/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p419/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p419/r3.claim: Zarkashi lists min in the two phrases about hearts hardened from God's remembrance and being unaware of this as meaning ʿan, about or away from.
BURHAN:v4p419/r3.anchor: الثامن بمعنى عن نحو ﴿ فويل للقاسية قلوبهم من ذكر الله ﴾

BURHAN:v4p419/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p419/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p419/r4.claim: An alternative analysis takes min in both phrases as marking the starting point.

BURHAN:v2p185/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p185/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p185/r3.claim: The missing comparison after the question is indicated by the following woe for hardened hearts: is the one whose chest God opened like one whose heart hardened?
BURHAN:v2p185/r3.anchor: وقد يومئ إلى المحذوف إما متأخر كقوله تعالى ﴿ أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام ﴾ فإنه لم يجئ له جواب فى اللفظ

BURHAN:v3p138/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p138/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p138/r6.claim: The predicate and comparison are omitted: is one whose chest is opened better than one made constricted and hard-hearted? The following warning signals the contrast.
BURHAN:v3p138/r6.anchor: أي أهذا خير أمن جعل صدره ضيقا حرجا وقسا قلبه

BURHAN:v3p167/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p167/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p167/r1.claim: The comparison leaves its counterpart unstated: one whose heart Allah hardened; the following warning about hard hearts makes the omission clear.
BURHAN:v3p167/r1.anchor: أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام كمن أقسى قلبه فحذف لدلالة

BURHAN:v3p167/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p167/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p167/r3.claim: Objects of شاء are often omitted when their content is implied by the answer; the estimate is “if God willed to do that, He would.”
BURHAN:v3p167/r3.anchor: والحكمة في كثرة حذف مفعول المشيئة المستلزمة لمضمون الجواب

BURHAN:v3p167/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p167/r4.speaker: ابن النحوية
BURHAN:v3p167/r4.claim: Ibn al-Nahwiyya conditions omission of the object on a conditional particle preceding it.
BURHAN:v3p167/r4.anchor: وشرط ابن النحوية 5 في حذفه دخول أداة الشرط عليه كما سبق

BURHAN:v3p167/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p167/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p167/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari, Ibn al-Zamalkani, and al-Tanukhi allow regular omission of the object of إرادة as with مشيئة; the response supplies its implied content.
BURHAN:v3p167/r5.anchor: صرح به الزمخشري في تفسير سورة البقرة وابن الزملكاني في البرهان

BURHAN:v2p350/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p350/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p350/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari alternates between placing the interrogative hamza before a conjunction and making it govern an omitted clause; the author prefers the hamza before the conjunction.
BURHAN:v2p350/r1.anchor: وتارة يجعلها متقدمة على العاطف كما ذكرناه وهو الأولى

BURHAN:v2p350/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p350/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p350/r2.claim: The omitted-verb analysis cannot work in examples such as “أو من ينشأ في الحلية,” “أفمن يعلم,” and “أفمن هو قائم.”
BURHAN:v2p350/r2.anchor: لا يمكن فيها تقدير فعل قبلها كقوله تعالى ﴿ أو من ينشأ في الحلية ﴾

BURHAN:v2p350/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p350/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p350/r6.claim: A conditional construction pairs two clauses, with the first verbal so it suits the condition.
BURHAN:v2p350/r6.anchor: المجازاة إنما تنعقد بين جملتين أولاهما فعلية لتلائم الشرط

BURHAN:v2p350/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p350/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p350/r7.claim: The apodosis may be nominal, verbal (jussive or not), adverbial, or itself conditional; joined to the protasis, the first is the condition and the second its answer, also called antecedent and consequent.
BURHAN:v2p350/r7.anchor: وثانيهما قد تكون اسمية وقد تكون فعلية جازمة وغير جازمة

SULAMI:v2p195#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r1.claim: One account sets out stages of faith: opening and illumination, testing, love and adornment, inscription and purification, knowledge of God’s oneness and transcendence, then verbal affirmation, action, and steadfastness.
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : الإيمان خمسة ثم خمسة أولا الشرح والتنوير لقوله : ﴿ أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام ﴾ ثم الامتحان لقوله : أولئك الذين امتحن الله قلوبهم للتقوى

SULAMI:v2p195#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r2.speaker: السيارى
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r2.claim: Al-Sayyārī traces Islam to faith, faith to knowledge, and knowledge to guidance and aid, which arise only through the opening and illumination of the breast.
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r2.anchor: قال السيارى : تولد الإسلام من الإيمان وتولد الإيمان من المعرفة وتولد المعرفة من الهداية والنصرة

SULAMI:v2p195#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r3.speaker: علي بن عبد الحميد
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r3.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd maps the inner person onto a lamp: the chest is its oil, the heart its wick, and the inner breast its flame; clean oil brightens the light.
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r3.anchor: وقال علي بن عبد الحميد : الصدر ساحة والفؤاد البيت والقلب بيت المخدع وفيه الضمير مثلها كمثل القنديل

SULAMI:v2p195#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r4.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r4.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī says God expanded the breast to bear the essence after it could bear the attributes.
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r4.anchor: قال الواسطي - رحمة الله عليه - : وسع الله صدره فاحتمل الذات بعد احتمال الصفات

SULAMI:v2p195#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r5.speaker: author
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r5.claim: The author describes this light as certainty in witnessing God through disappearance from the visible and unseen realms; after traversing every state, the knower receives an obscure address and reports only that people would weep more and laugh less.
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r5.anchor: على يقين من مشاهدة ربه بالغيبوبة عن الملك والملكوت فلم يبق عليه مقام إلا سلكه ولا حال إلى استوفاه

SULAMI:v2p195#3/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r6.speaker: عمرو المكي
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r6.claim: ʿAmr al-Makkī says the servant’s vision of the grandeur of divine oneness and lordship blinds them to every other object.
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r6.anchor: وقال عمرو المكي في هذه الآية هو وقوع نظر العبد على عظيم علم الوحدانية وجلال الربوبية

SULAMI:v2p195#3/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r7.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r7.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī says the light of the opening is an immense love borne only by those supported by divine solicitude and care, which protect bodies and spirits respectively.
SULAMI:v2p195#3/r7.anchor: قال الواسطي في قوله : ﴿ أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه ﴾ قال : نور الشرح محبة عظيمة

SULAMI:v2p196/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p196/r1.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p196/r1.claim: Al-Qāsim calls opening, illumination, and adornment the beginnings of faith, linking opening to the account of Ḥāritha.
SULAMI:v2p196/r1.anchor: قال القاسم : أوائل الإيمان الشرح والتنوير والتزيين والشرح في حديث حارثة

SULAMI:v2p196/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p196/r2.speaker: الترمذي
SULAMI:v2p196/r2.claim: Al-Tirmidhī says people of certainty affirm God in heart, word, and deed and fulfill this through the opening of the breast bestowed by God.
SULAMI:v2p196/r2.anchor: قال الترمذي : أهل اليقين وحدوا الله قلبا وقولا وفعلا ووفوا له ذلك بشرح الصدر الذي من به الله عليهم

SULAMI:v2p196/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p196/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p196/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ explains being on a light from one’s Lord as having clarification from Him.
SULAMI:v2p196/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : من آمن بالله وصدقه فهو على نور من ربه أي على بيان من ربه

SULAMI:v2p196/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p196/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p196/r4.claim: Another view says God made Himself known so they knew Him, showed them so they saw Him, then opened their hearts through seeing creation while turning their sight from all besides Him.
SULAMI:v2p196/r4.anchor: قال بعضهم : تعرف إليهم حتى عرفوه وبصرهم حتى ابصروه وذلك حين شرح قلوبهم برؤية الصنع واعمى ابصارهم عن النظر إلى سواه

SULAMI:v2p196/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p196/r5.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p196/r5.claim: Al-Qāsim interprets the light from God as faith in divine decree.
SULAMI:v2p196/r5.anchor: قال القاسم في قوله : ﴿ على نور من ربه ﴾ قال : الإيمان بالقدر

SULAMI:v2p196/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p196/r6.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p196/r6.claim: Al-Ḥusayn says hardness caused by blessings is worse than hardness from forgetfulness or hardship, since blessing should prompt gratitude and hardship remembrance.
SULAMI:v2p196/r6.anchor: قال الحسين : قسوة القلب بالنعم اشد من قسوته بالنسيان والشدة فإنه بالنعمة يشكر وبالشدة يذكر

SULAMI:v2p196/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p196/r7.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p196/r7.claim: Al-Ḥusayn cites a verse about receiving the punishment of arrogance after being boastful in the blessings of love.
SULAMI:v2p196/r7.anchor: وأنشد في معناه : قد كنت في نعمة الهوى بطرا … فأدركتني عقوبة البطر

SULAMI:v2p196/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p196/r8.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p196/r8.claim: Al-Ḥusayn says pursuing a permitted pleasure merely for enjoyment is punished by wasted life, hardness of heart, and worldly anxiety.
SULAMI:v2p196/r8.anchor: وقال : من هم بشيء مما اباحه العلم تلذذا عوقب بتضييع العمر وقسوة القلب وتعب الهم في الدنيا

SULAMI:v2p196/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p196/r9.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p196/r9.claim: He lists the heart’s punishments as rust, hardness, and blindness.
SULAMI:v2p196/r9.anchor: وقال : عقوبة القلب الران والقسوة والعمى

SULAMI:v2p196/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p196/r10.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v2p196/r10.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Muʿādh says hardness of heart comes from following desire.
SULAMI:v2p196/r10.anchor: قال يحيى بن معاذ : قسوة القلب من اتباع الهوى

ITQAN:v4p410#6/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p410#6/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد
ITQAN:v4p410#6/r1.claim: Al-Hakim reports from Abu Sa‘id that reciting Surat al-Kahf on Friday brings light from that Friday to the next.
ITQAN:v4p410#6/r1.anchor: أخرج الحاكم من حديث أبي سعيد ( من قرأ سورة الكهف في يوم الجمعة

ITQAN:v4p410#6/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p410#6/r2.speaker: أبو الدرداء
ITQAN:v4p410#6/r2.claim: Muslim reports from Abu al-Darda’ that memorizing ten opening verses of al-Kahf protects from the Dajjal.
ITQAN:v4p410#6/r2.anchor: وأخرج مسلم من حديث أبي الدرداء ( من حفظ عشر آيات من أول سورة الكهف

ITQAN:v4p410#6/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p410#6/r3.speaker: معاذ بن أنس
ITQAN:v4p410#6/r3.claim: Ahmad reports that reciting al-Kahf’s opening and ending gives light from foot to head, while the whole surah gives light between earth and heaven.
ITQAN:v4p410#6/r3.anchor: وأخرج أحمد من حديث معاذ بن أنس ( من قرأ أول سورة الكهف وآخرها كانت

ITQAN:v4p410#6/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p410#6/r4.speaker: عمر
ITQAN:v4p410#6/r4.claim: Al-Bazzar reports from Umar that reciting “Whoever hopes to meet his Lord” at night gives light from Aden to Mecca, filled with angels.

ITQAN:v4p439#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r1.speaker: ابن التين
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r1.claim: Ibn al-Tin calls healing recitation with protective surahs and divine names spiritual medicine; through the righteous it heals by God’s permission, and its scarcity led people to bodily medicine.
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن التين الرقي بالمعوذات وغيرها من أسماء الله تعالى هو الطب الروحاني إذا كان على لسان الأبرار

ITQAN:v4p439#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r2.claim: The author cites a saying that a person with firm conviction could recite the protective surahs over a mountain and make it move.
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r2.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( لو أن رجلا موقنا قرأ بها على جبل لزال

ITQAN:v4p439#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r3.speaker: القرطبي
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r3.claim: Al-Qurtubi permits ruqyah with God’s words and names, and recommends it when transmitted.
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r3.anchor: وقال القرطبي تجوز الرقية بكلام الله وأسمائه فإن كان مأثورا استحب

ITQAN:v4p439#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r4.speaker: الشافعي
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r4.claim: Al-Shafi‘i permits ruqyah with the Book of God and familiar remembrance of God.
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r4.anchor: وقال الربيع سألت الشافعي عن الرقية فقال لا بأس أن يرقى بكتاب الله وما يعرف من ذكر الله

ITQAN:v4p439#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r5.speaker: ابن بطال
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r5.claim: Ibn Battal says the protective surahs gather prayers against magic, envy, Satan, and its whispering, explaining the Prophet’s reliance on them.
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن بطال في المعوذات سر ليس في غيرها من القرآن لما اشتملت عليه من جوامع الدعاء

ITQAN:v4p439#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r6.speaker: ابن القيم
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim says al-Fatiha gathers monotheism, guidance, worship, repentance, and heart-reform, making it apt for healing every illness.
ITQAN:v4p439#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن القيم في حديث الرقية بالفاتحة إذا ثبت أن لبعض الكلام خواص ومنافع فما الظن بكلام رب العالمين

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p265/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p265/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p265/r1.claim: The poet treats the moon’s effect on linen as a known fact: he explains the garment’s rapid wear by saying its buttons have been fastened onto the moon.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p265/r1.anchor: قد عمد كما ترى إلى شيء هو خاصية في طبيعة القمر وأمر غريب من تأثيره ثم جعل يرى أن قوما انكروا بلى الكتان بسرعة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p265/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p265/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p265/r2.claim: The simile is so suppressed that the poem argues from the moon as though it were literally involved; making the comparison explicit would weaken the image and destroy its proof against wonder.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p265/r2.anchor: وأن التشبيه قد نسى وانسى وصار كما يقول الشيخ أبو على فيما يتعلق به الطرف إنه شريعة منسوخة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p265/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p265/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p265/r3.claim: Another poet attributes linen’s wear to constant moonlight, but his wording does not claim the moon’s causal role as forcefully as the first poem.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p265/r3.anchor: إلا أن لفظة لا ينبىء عن القوة التي لهذا البيت في دعوى القمر

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p265/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p265/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p265/r4.claim: Al-Abbas ibn al-Ahnaf likewise makes the metaphorical claim that the beloved is the sun seem factual, then consoles the heart because her dwelling is in the sky.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p265/r4.anchor: قول العباس بن الأحنف ( هي الشمس مسكنها في السماء فعز الفؤاد عزاء جميلا )

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369/r1.claim: The verse concerns Hamza and Ali, whose hearts God opened to Islam, and Abu Lahab and his sons, whose hearts hardened against God’s remembrance.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p369/r1.anchor: نزلت في حمزة وعلي وأبي لهب وولده، فعلي وحمزة ممن شرح الله صدره

NAHHAS:v4p8/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p8/r6.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v4p8/r6.claim: Abu Ishaq calls the fāʾ a result or consequence particle.
NAHHAS:v4p8/r6.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق هذه الفاء فاء المجازاة

NAHHAS:v4p8/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p8/r7.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v4p8/r7.claim: Al-Mubarrad glosses قسا as hardening; عتا and عسا are close, and a hard heart does not soften.
NAHHAS:v4p8/r7.anchor: قال محمد بن يزيد يقال قسا إذا صلب قال وكذلك عتا وعسا مقاربة لها

NAHHAS:v4p8/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p8/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p8/r8.claim: أولئك is a nominative subject referring to those whose hearts hardened; في ضلال مبين is its predicate.
NAHHAS:v4p8/r8.anchor: ( أولئك ) في موضع رفع بالابتداء أي أولئك الذين

SAMIN-DURR:39:22/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:22/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:22/r1.claim: The missing comparison is one with a hardened heart or a hard-hearted person who turns away.
SAMIN-DURR:39:22/r1.anchor: والتقدير: أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام كمن قسا قلبه، أو كالقاسي المعرض، لدلالة { فويل للقاسية قلوبهم } عليه.

SAMIN-DURR:39:22/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:39:22/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:39:22/r2.claim: The ellipsis parallels أفمن يتقي in 39:24 and أفمن حق in 39:19.

ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r7.claim: The fāʾ marks the result, and the comparison's answer is omitted: one guided by God is unlike one whose heart is sealed and hardened.
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r7.anchor: فهذه الفاء فاء المجازاة، والمعنى أفمن شرح الله صدره فاهتدى كمن طبع على قلبه

ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r8.claim: With min, the phrase means that whenever God's remembrance is recited to them, their hearts become hard, as in the verse about increasing sickness.
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r8.anchor: فمن قال من ذكر الله، فالمعنى كلما تلي عليه ذكر الله قسا قلبه

ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r9.claim: With ʿan, the phrase means their hearts have become hard and harsh toward accepting God's remembrance.
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r9.anchor: ومن قال: عن ذكر الله فالمعنى أنه غلظ قلبه وجفا عن قبول ذكر الله

ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r10.claim: “Those” in manifest error refers to the people whose hearts are hardened.
ZAJJAJ:v4p350/r10.anchor: أولئك في ضلال مبين). يعني القاسية قلوبهم

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p541/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p541/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p541/r1.claim: The Qur’an is a great favour: receptive people are moved by it, while the stone-hearted are deprived of it and face destruction like messenger-denying nations.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p541/r1.anchor: The stone-hearted, however, will be deprived from the Qur’ān and will face the punishment of destruction

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r8.claim: The author signals that one aspect of the example will be explained in the next verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p543/r8.anchor: one particular aspect shall be explained in the next verse.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r1.claim: As with rain on land, the Qur’an benefits people according to their capacities: receptive hearts flourish, while those hardened after wasting their abilities remain barren and face doom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r1.anchor: Similarly, the rain of the Qur’ān will also not benefit each person to the same extent:

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r2.claim: The predicate of the interrogative sentence is suppressed and supplied in the author’s translation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r2.anchor: The enunciative (khabar) in this interrogative sentence is suppressed which I have unveiled in the translation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r3.claim: “From the remembrance of God” means that their hearts remained hard despite God’s reminders to them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p544/r3.anchor: whose hearts in spite of being reminded by God remained rock-hard.

NASHR:v1p18/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p18/r2.speaker: مكي بن أبي طالب
NASHR:v1p18/r2.claim: Makkī divides readings into three groups: documented transmission, orally acquired readings absent from books, and the smallest group inferred by analogy when no transmission exists.
NASHR:v1p18/r2.anchor: فجميع ما ذكرناه في هذا الكتاب ينقسم ثلاثة أقسام

NASHR:v1p18/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p18/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p18/r3.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī rejects extending analogy indiscriminately from transmitted to untransmitted or from weak to strong readings, including showing the converted mīm of nūn and tanwīn.
NASHR:v1p18/r3.anchor: وقد زل بسبب ذلك قوم وأطلقوا قياس ما لا يروى على ما روي

NASHR:v1p18/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p18/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p18/r4.claim: He rejects claims to lighten a still rāʾ before kasra or yāʾ without a transmitted basis.
NASHR:v1p18/r4.anchor: وقطع بعض القراء بترقيق الراء الساكنة قبل الكسرة والياء

NASHR:v1p18/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p18/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p18/r5.claim: He rejects lightening the lām of the divine name by analogy with the light rāʾ in dhikr Allāh.
NASHR:v1p18/r5.anchor: وإجازة بعض من بلغنا عنه ترقيق لام الجلالة

NASHR:v2p450/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p450/r1.speaker: الآمدي
NASHR:v2p450/r1.claim: A report in al-Furūʿ says not to recite al-Fātiḥa and five verses of al-Baqara; al-Āmidī explains the restriction as applying before supplication, while another view recommends the practice.

NASHR:v2p450/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p450/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p450/r2.claim: Ibn al-Jazarī interprets Aḥmad’s ‘no’ as forbidding the extra recitation before supplication; supplication should follow Sūrat al-Nās, though another report from Aḥmad recommends it.
NASHR:v2p450/r2.anchor: يكون دعاؤه عقيب قراءة سورة الناس

NASHR:v2p450/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p450/r3.speaker: السخاوي
NASHR:v2p450/r3.claim: Al-Sakhāwī asks how the report that no deed saves from Hell more than remembrance of God fits with the report that the Qurʾān is the best remembrance.
NASHR:v2p450/r3.anchor: قال السخاوي بعد ذكر هذا الحديث: فإن قيل

NASHR:v2p450/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p450/r4.speaker: السخاوي
NASHR:v2p450/r4.claim: Al-Sakhāwī answers that the Qurʾān is remembrance because it praises God and recounts His mercy, power, creation, care, guidance, laws, and the fates of opponents; all of it is His speech.
NASHR:v2p450/r4.anchor: القرآن من ذكر الله إذ فيه الثناء على الله عز وجل ومدحه

NASHR:v2p450/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p450/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p450/r5.claim: The author cites sound reports naming faith, jihad, pilgrimage, prayer, honoring parents, patience, generosity, and fasting among the best deeds.
NASHR:v2p450/r5.anchor: ورد في هذا المعنى أحاديث صحيحة منها أنه

NASHR:v2p450/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p450/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p450/r6.claim: One harmonization takes ‘best’ to mean one among several deeds in the highest rank, rather than a single exclusive deed.
NASHR:v2p450/r6.anchor: إن المراد أي من أفضل الأعمال النظائر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r1.claim: The promise to the God-fearing contrasts with the preceding punishment of unbelievers; لكن between the groups urges piety.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r1.anchor: ولما ذكر حال الكفار في النار، وأن الخاسرين لهم ظلل، ذكر حال المؤمنين، وناسب الاستدراك هنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r12.claim: The verse was revealed concerning Hamza and Ali.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r12.anchor: أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام: نزلت في حمزة، وعلي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r13.claim: من is a subject with an omitted predicate inferred from the following woe; Abu Lahab and his son exemplified hard hearts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r13.anchor: ومن مبتدأ، وخبره محذوف يدل عليه فويل للقاسية قلوبهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r14.claim: Opening the breast is a metaphor for accepting faith, goodness, light, and guidance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r14.anchor: وشرح الصدر استعارة عن قبوله للإيمان والخير والنور والهداية.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r15.speaker: الحديث
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r15.claim: A hadith says the heart expands when light enters it; its signs are turning toward the eternal home, shunning delusion, and preparing for death before death.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r15.anchor: وفي الحديث: «كيف انشراح الصدور؟ قال: إذا دخل النور القلب انشرح وانفسح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r16.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r16.claim: من ذكر الله means because of God's remembrance: when God is mentioned to them, their hearts harden.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r16.anchor: فويل للقاسية قلوبهم من ذكر الله: أي من أجل ذكره، أي إذا ذكر الله عندهم قست قلوبهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r17.speaker: مالك بن دينار
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r17.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says no servant has been struck with a punishment greater than a hard heart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r17.anchor: وقال مالك بن دينار: ما ضرب عبد بعقوبة أعظم من قسوة قلب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r18.claim: أولئك refers to the hard-hearted, and their manifest error is an evident confusion that an observer cannot miss.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p193/r18.anchor: أولئك: أي القاسية قلوبهم، في ضلال مبين: أي في حيرة واضحة، لا تخفى على من تأملها.

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r1.claim: The verse resumes the discussion and explains why remembrance is specially received by people of understanding.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r1.anchor: استئناف جلر مجرى التعليل لما قبله من تخصيص الذكرى بأولي الألباب

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r2.claim: “Expansion” literally means spreading or extending flesh; figuratively it means capaciousness, and here God's creation of the rational soul with complete readiness to accept Islam.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r2.anchor: الشرح في الأصل البسط والمد للحم ونحوه ويكنى به عن التسويع وتجوز به هنا عن خلق النفس الناطقة

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r3.claim: The chest stands for the rational soul by way of the heart in which it first attaches through a subtle vapor from refined nourishment, then governs and directs the body; this soul bears Islam and faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r3.anchor: من حيث أنه محل للقلب وفي تجويفه بخار لطيف يتكون من صفوة الأغذية وبه تتعلق النفس أولا

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r4.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r4.claim: Some eminent scholars classify “God expanded his chest” as a representational metaphor.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r4.anchor: وجعل بعض الأجلة شرح الله صدره استعارة تمثيلية

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r5.claim: The interrogative hamza denies an omitted premise; the fa coordinates to that premise and the predicate of “who” is omitted but supplied by what follows: are all people equal?
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r5.anchor: لدلالة ما بعده عليه والتقدير أكل الناس سواء فمن شرح الله

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r6.claim: The expanded person was created ready for Islam and remains upon original human disposition, unchanged by acquired corrupting influences.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r6.anchor: وخلقه مستعدا للإسلام فبقي على الفطرة الأصلية ولم تتغير بالعوارض المكتسبة القادحة فيها

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r7.claim: The light is God's grace shining from the towers of mercy, enabling him to recognize the signs in creation and revelation and follow them to truth.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r7.anchor: وهو اللطف الإلهي المشرق عليه من بروج الرحمة عند مشاهدة الآيات التكوينية والتنزيلية

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r8.claim: Alusi also allows that the light may be a divine reality distinct from grace and enabling guidance, by which truth is apprehended.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r8.anchor: وقد يقال : هو أمر إلهي غير اللطف والتوفيق يدرك به الحق

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r9.claim: By bad choice, the opposite person replaces God's original disposition, hardens the heart, constricts the chest, falls under error's darkness, and turns wholly away from signs without remembering or benefiting from them.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r9.anchor: كمن قسا قلبه وحرج صدره بتبديل فطرة الله تعالى بسوء اختياره وستولى عليه ظلمات الغي والضلال

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r10.claim: The wording “upon a light” rather than “has a light” depicts continued, settled residence in light, a metaphor for grace and guidance.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r10.anchor: للدلالة على استمرار ذلك واستقراره في النور وهو مستعار للطف والتوفيق للإهتداء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r11.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet explained an expanded heart as one into which light enters and which then opens; its signs are longing for the eternal home, detachment from the delusive world, and preparing for death before it arrives.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r11.anchor: وجاء برواية الثعلبي في تفسيره والحاكم في مستدركه والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان وابن مردويه عن ابن مسعود أنه قال

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r12.claim: Alusi resolves the report's apparent reversal of the verse's order by distinguishing innate readiness in the verse from later expansion after grace in the report; guidance has prior and later stages, and the answer uses the wise redirection of a question.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r12.anchor: والظاهر أن السؤال عما في الآية وأن الجواب بيان لكيفيته وأجيب بأن الإهتداء له مراتب بعضها مقدم وبعضها مؤخر

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r13.claim: “Because of God's remembrance” means that mentioning God or His signs should soften hearts, but these people recoil and grow harder.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r13.anchor: أي من أجل ذكره سبحانه الذي حقه أن تلين منه القلوب أي إذا ذكر الله تعالى عندهم أو آياته عز وجل اشمأزوا من ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r14.claim: A variant reads “away from God's remembrance”; the transmitted “because of” is stronger, since those hardened because of it resist acceptance more than those hardened for another reason.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r14.anchor: وقريء ( عن ذكر الله ) والمتواترة أبلغ لأن القاسي من أجل الشيء أشد تأبيا من قبوله

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r15.claim: Mentioning chest expansion for believers and heart-hardness for rejecters intensifies the contrast: the believer's acceptance overflows the heart to fill the chest, while the hard heart admits nothing.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r15.anchor: ذكر شرح الصدر لأن توسعته وجعله محلا للإسلام دون القلب الذي فيه يدل على شدته وإفراط كثرته

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r16.claim: Attributing expansion to God signals its fullest form, as the act of an omnipotent, wise agent.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r16.anchor: وإسناده إلى الله تعالى الظاهر في أنه على أتم الوجوه لأنه فعل قادر حكيم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r17.claim: The counterpart is hardness rather than tightness: like a solid rock, hardness accepts nothing, whereas tightness suggests accepting at least a little.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r17.anchor: وقابله بالقساوة مع أن مقتضى المقابلة أن يعبر بالضيق لأن القساوة كما في الصخرة الصماء تقتضي عدم قبول شيء

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r18.claim: The text does not explicitly attribute their hardness to God's making it, implying that it clings so deeply it would arise from their own natures even without being created.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r18.anchor: وعدل عن التعبير بما يفيد مجعولية القساوة له تعالى وخلقه إياها للإشارة إلى غاية لزومها لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r19.claim: Hardness is assigned to hearts rather than chests because the heart is the organ whose corruption corrupts the whole body.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r19.anchor: وأما إسنادها إلى القلوب دون الصدور فللتنصيص على فساد هذا العضو الذي إذا فسد فسد الجسد كله

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r20.claim: The believer is singular but the unbelievers plural to suggest that believers, though many, are like one person, unlike the unbelievers.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r20.anchor: للإشارة إلى أن المؤمنين وأن تعددوا كرجل واحد ولا كذلك الكفار

ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r21.claim: “Those” points to the distant ones characterized by hard hearts, who are in manifest error.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p257/r21.anchor: أولئك ( البعداء المتصفون بما ذكر من قسوة القلوب ( في ضلال مبين

ALUSI-FULL:v23p258/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258/r1.claim: Alusi says the verse was revealed about Ali and Hamza, whose chests God expanded for Islam, and Abu Lahab and his son, whose hearts were hard.
ALUSI-FULL:v23p258/r1.anchor: والآية نزلت في علي وحمزة رضي الله تعالى عنهما وأبي لهب وابنه فعلي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وحمزة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r4.claim: God expands the person's breast to accept the truth; being on light from God is unlike having a hardened heart.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r4.anchor: وسعه لقبول الحق، {فهو على نور من ربه} ليس كمن أقسى الله قلبه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r5.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet said light entering the heart makes it expand; its signs are turning toward the eternal home, shunning the deceptive home, and preparing for death before it arrives.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p114/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115/r1.speaker: مالك بن دينار
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115/r1.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says no punishment inflicted on a servant is worse than a hard heart, and God has never been angry with a people without removing mercy from them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p115/r1.anchor: قال مالك بن دينار: ما ضرب عبد بعقوبة أعظم من قسوة قلب،

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r5.claim: God has made such a person receptive to Islam with ease, creating a strong readiness to accept it without resistance; the chest houses the heart and the soul's receptivity.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r5.anchor: حتى تمكن فيه بيسر عبر به عمن خلق نفسه شديدة الاستعداد

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r6.claim: The light is knowledge and guidance to the truth.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r7.claim: A Prophetic report says that when light enters the heart it expands; its sign is turning toward the eternal home, renouncing the deceptive world, and preparing for death before it arrives.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r7.anchor: إذا دخل النور القلب انشرح وانفسح، فقيل فما علامة ذلك

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r8.claim: The predicate of man is omitted and supplied by the following warning. Min means “because of God's remembrance,” stronger than “away from it”: hardness caused by the reminder is greater refusal than hardness for another cause.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r8.anchor: من أجل ذكره وهو أبلغ من أن يكون عن مكان من

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r9.claim: The contrast magnifies the receptive and the resistant: God is said to open the first person's chest, while the second's hard heart is attributed to the person himself.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r9.anchor: وأسنده إلى الله وقابله بقساوة القلب وأسنده إليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r10.claim: Their error is manifest to anyone who gives it even a brief look.

BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r11.claim: The verse was revealed about Ḥamza, ʿAlī, Abū Lahab, and his son.
BAYDAWI-FULL:39:21-22/r11.anchor: والآية نزلت في حمزة وعلي وأبي لهب وولده

BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r11.speaker: author
