BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r11.claim: The rhetorical question follows the claim that only clear minds perceive the sign: God opens the heart to Islam by making it soft and responsive to evidence.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r11.anchor: أفمن شرح الله } أي الذي له القدرة الكاملة والعلم الشامل { صدره للإسلام } أي للانقياد للدليل

BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r12.claim: The surrendered believer stands on the light of the Book, a great clarification that he takes from, gives through, and returns to in every matter.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p436/r12.anchor: فهو } أي فيتسبب عن إسلام ظاهره وباطنه للداعي أن كان { على نور } أي بيان عظيم كتاب , به يأخذ

BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r1.claim: His Lord is the benefactor who graciously guided him; he is blessed and follows a straight path.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r1.anchor: { من ربه } أي المحسن إليه إحسانه في انقياده , فبشرى له فهو على صراط مستقيم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r2.claim: The opposite is a constricted heart, hard and stumbling in darkness; the wording gives woe to the hard-hearted in place of an explicit description of a constricted breast.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r2.anchor: كمن جعل صدره ضيقا حرجا فكان قلبه قاسيا , فكان في الظلام خابطا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r3.claim: “Hard-hearted” stands for constriction of the breast, with the sentence compressing the contrast that was expected from the preceding clause.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r3.anchor: هكذا كان الأصل ولكن قيل : { فويل للقاسية قلوبهم } أي لضيق صدورهم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r4.claim: Their hardness begins at God’s remembrance, which should reassure hearts and soften skin; resisting praise of the One encompassing all perfect names and attributes makes them harder than stone.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r4.anchor: { من ذكر الله } فإن من تبتدئ قسوته مما تطمئن به القلوب وتلين له الجلود

BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r5.claim: Those far removed are in manifest error, clear in itself and making their condition apparent to everyone.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r5.anchor: { أولئك } أي الأباعد الأباغض { في ضلال مبين * } أي واضح في نفسه موضح أمره لكل واحد

BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r6.claim: The verse uses ḥitbāk: the opening and light in the first half imply their opposites in the second, while woe and misguidance imply what is omitted from the first.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r6.anchor: الآية من الاحتباك : ذكر أولا الشرح والنور دليلا على حذف ضده ثانيا , وثانيا الويل للقاسي والضلال دليلا على حذف أولا

BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r7.speaker: النبي ﷺ
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r7.claim: In a report from Ibn Masʿūd, the Prophet says the heart opens when light enters it; its sign is turning toward the eternal home, leaving the deluding world, and preparing for death before it arrives.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r7.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ هذه الآية , قال : فقلنا : يا رسول الله ؟ كيف انشراح صدورهم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r8.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r8.claim: Al-Qushayrī describes ascending lights: knowledge, understanding, certainty, unveiling of attributes, witnessing, then the realities of divine unity that eclipse all earlier lights.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r8.anchor: وقال الأستاذ أبوة القاسم القشيري : والنور الذي من قبله سبحانه نور اللوائح بنجوم العلم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r9.speaker: القشيري
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r9.claim: Al-Qushayrī’s cited saying compares growing insight to moonlit stars and then to dawn: when the sun appears, its light absorbs the stars’ lesser brightness.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p437/r9.anchor: المؤمن بقوة عقله يوجب استقلاله بعمله إلى أن يبدو ومنه كمال تمكنه من وقادة بصيرته

DURR-FULL:v7p218/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r5.claim: Mujahid says the person whose breast God has opened is unlike those whose hearts are hardened.
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام} الآية قال: ليس المشروح صدره كالقاسية قلوبهم

DURR-FULL:v7p218/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r6.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r6.claim: Qatada reports that the Prophet said the breast does open and gave its sign as turning toward the lasting abode, shunning worldly deception, and preparing for death before it comes.
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r6.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه} قالوا: يا رسول الله فهل ينفرج الصدر

DURR-FULL:v7p218/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r7.claim: Ibn Masud reports the Prophet explaining that when light enters the heart it expands; its sign is turning to the eternal abode, avoiding worldly deception, and preparing for death.
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال: تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية {أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام

DURR-FULL:v7p218/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r8.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r8.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the wisest believer remembers death most and prepares best for it; the Prophet says light makes the heart spacious and gives the signs of an opened breast.
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r8.anchor: في نوادر الأصول عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما

DURR-FULL:v7p218/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر عبد الله بن المسور
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r9.claim: A report from Abu Jaʿfar Abd Allah ibn al-Miswar attributes a similar teaching to the Messenger, adding this verse about the opened breast and light.
DURR-FULL:v7p218/r9.anchor: ثم أخرج عن أبي جعفر عبد الله بن المسور عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نحوه وزاد فيه {أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام

DURR-FULL:v7p220/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r1.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet warning that excessive speech without remembrance hardens the heart and that the hard-hearted are farthest from God.
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: لا تكثروا الكلام بغير ذكر الله

DURR-FULL:v7p220/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r2.speaker: أبو الجلد
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r2.claim: Abu al-Jald says Jesus advised the disciples that speech without remembrance hardens hearts and leaves the hard-hearted far from God, though they do not realize it.
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r2.anchor: عن أبي الجلد رضي الله عنه أن عيسى عليه السلام أوصى إلى الحواريين: أن لا تكثروا الكلام بغير ذكر الله

DURR-FULL:v7p220/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r3.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r3.claim: Ali reports the Prophet saying that servants' eating and sleeping bring hardness to their hearts.
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r3.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أكل العباد ونومهم عليه قسوة في قلوبهم

DURR-FULL:v7p220/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r4.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r4.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet advising people to accompany food with remembrance and prayer and not sleep after eating, lest their hearts harden.
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r4.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: أذيبوا طعامكم بذكر الله والصلاة ولا تناموا عليه

DURR-FULL:v7p220/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r5.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r5.claim: Aisha reports that love of food, sleep, and ease are three traits that produce hardness of heart.
DURR-FULL:v7p220/r5.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: يورث القسوة في القلب ثلاث خصال حب الطعام وحب النوم

IBNHIBBAN:814/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:814/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن بسر
IBNHIBBAN:814/r1.claim: Ibn Busr reports that when a Bedouin asked for a practice to hold fast to, the Prophet advised keeping one's tongue continually moist with remembrance of God.
IBNHIBBAN:814/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن بسر، قال: جاء

IBNHIBBAN:818/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:818/r1.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNHIBBAN:818/r1.claim: Muadh reports that, when he asked which deeds God loves most, the Prophet answered that one should die with a tongue moist from remembrance of God.
IBNHIBBAN:818/r1.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل، قال: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r2.claim: The rain and growth passage begins the sūra’s Qur’an-and-Islam guidance theme, resumed in 39:22–23 after the excursus beginning at 39:2.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r2.anchor: استئناف ابتدائي انتقل به إلى غرض التنويه بالقرآن وما احتوى عليه من هدى الإسلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r8.claim: The juxtaposition of the rain parable with 39:22–23 signals the lesson drawn from it: the Qur’an-guided response parallels the growth of vegetation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p375/r8.anchor: إشارة إلى العبرة من هذا التمثيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r2.claim: The rhetorical question follows from the contrast with the God-fearing promised chambers in 39:20 and the preceding parable of benefiting from the Qur’an.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r3.claim: The relative pronoun “whoever” is the subject, with an omitted predicate inferred from the contrast: like the one condemned to punishment in the darkness of unbelief, or like the one whose heart is hard.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r3.anchor: مما اقتضاه حرف الاستدراك من مخالفة حالة لحال من حق عليه كلمة العذاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r4.claim: “Expanding the breast for Islam” metaphorically means the mind accepts and loves Islam; literal breast-opening is likened to relieving the constriction that confusion and distress produce in breathing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r4.anchor: وشرح الصدر للإسلام استعارة لقبول العقل هدي الإسلام ومحبته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r5.claim: The Qur’an’s elegant choice of “expand” captures the happiness, confidence, resilience, and freedom from doubt that Islamic teaching and character give the believer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p379/r5.anchor: لأن تعاليم الإسلام وأخلاقه وآدابه تكسب المسلم فرحا بحاله ومسرة برضى ربه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r1.claim: Islam lifts the believer above idolatry, forms wisdom, noble and sincere conduct, brotherhood, contentment, patience, hope, and gratitude; confidence in God makes him clear-sighted, brave, and dignified.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r1.anchor: فكان صدره منشرحا بالإسلام متلقيا الحوادث باستبصار غير هياب شجاع القلب عزيز النفس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r2.claim: The lām is causal: God expanded his breast for the sake of Islam, meaning for its acceptance.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r3.claim: The pronoun in “he is upon light” refers back to “whoever” whose breast God expanded.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r4.claim: Light is a metaphor for guidance and clarity of truth: it reveals things and removes darkness and confusion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r4.anchor: مستعار للهدى ووضوح الحق لأن النور به تنجلي الأشياء ويخرج المبصر من غياهب الضلالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r5.claim: “Upon” is metaphorically used for being firmly established in light, as in 2:5.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r5.anchor: واستعيرت { على } استعارة تبعية أو تمثيلية للتمكن من النور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r6.claim: “From his Lord” modifies “light”; min marks its origin, so this is complete divine light without darkness, like the light God guides people to in 24:35.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r6.anchor: أي نور موصوف بأنه جاء به من عند الله فهو نور كامل لا تخالطه ظلمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r7.claim: Those whose breasts were not expanded have innate hard hearts through which the call to good cannot enter; “woe” summarizes their extreme misery and wretchedness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r7.anchor: يدل على حال ضده وهم الذين لم يشرح الله صدورهم للإسلام فكانت لقلوبهم قساوة فطروا عليها فلا تسلك دعوة الخير إلى قلوبهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r8.claim: “Woe” conveys the utmost misery and wretchedness, a sense detailed at 2:79.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p380/r8.anchor: وقد تقدم تفصيل معانيه عند قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r1.claim: Hardness literally means thickness and solidity in bodies; hard hearts metaphorically mean minds little affected by admonitions, while softness denotes quick receptiveness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r1.anchor: مستعارة لقلة تأثر العقل بما يسدى إلى صاحبه من المواعظ ونحوها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r2.speaker: مغني اللبيب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r2.claim: Mughni al-Labib treats min as equivalent to ʿan (“away from/about”), citing this verse and 50:22.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAshur finds the “min means ʿan” analysis unnecessary: here min can mark cause, as al-Zamakhshari says, and in 50:22 it marks a starting point.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r3.anchor: وفيه نظر ، لإمكان حملهما على معنيين شائعين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r4.claim: “Remembrance of God” here means the Qur’an, and its attribution to God honors it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r4.anchor: والمراد بذكر الله القرآن وإضافته إلى الله زيادة تشريف له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r5.claim: When a Qur’anic verse is recited, the disbelievers recoil; the resulting aversion settles in them and hardens their hearts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r5.anchor: أنهم إذا تليت آية اشمأزوا فتمكن الاشمئزاز منهم فقست قلوبهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r6.claim: Their unbelief makes them hate the Qur’anic call to Islam; repeated avoidance and resistance entrench that hatred until their hearts become hard.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r6.anchor: فكلما سمعوه أعرضوا وعاندوا وتجددت كراهية الإسلام في قلوبهم حتى ترسخ تلك الكراهية في قلوبهم فتصير قلوبهم قاسية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r7.claim: The same remembrance that brings believers’ hearts tranquility can harden disbelievers’ hearts because effects vary with receptivity; a sound heart softens, while obstinacy and pride deepen the disease.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p381/r7.anchor: وسبب ذلك اختلاف القابلية فإن السبب الواحد تختلف آثاره وأفعاله باختلاف القابلية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r1.claim: The statement is an explanatory resumption answering why mention of God hardens their hearts: they are so immersed in misguidance that hearing it cannot dispel their error.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r1.anchor: مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا لأن ما قبله من الحكم بأن قساوة قلوبهم من أجل أن يذكر الله عندهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r2.claim: The demonstrative after their hard-heartedness marks them as deserving their ensuing state; severe misguidance causes hardness and is also its consequence, as psychological causes and effects can reciprocate without temporal circularity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r2.anchor: وافتتاح هذه الجملة باسم الإشارة عقب ما وصفوا به من قساوة القلوب لإفادة أن ما سيذكر من حالهم بعد الإشارة إليهم صاروا به أحرياء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r3.claim: Mubin means intense and unmistakable; it is figurative for firmly rooted misguidance, evident to a reflective observer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r3.anchor: فالمبين كناية عن القوة والرسوخ فهو يبين للمتأمل أنه ضلال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r4.claim: The next passage explains that Qur’anic guidance softens God-fearing hearts; hardness comes from inner rust, as with the sealed hearts in 2:6–7, not from any shortcoming in the Qur’an’s guidance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v23p382/r4.anchor: مبينة أن قساوة قلوب الضالين من سماع القرآن إنما هي لرين في قلوبهم وعقولهم لا لنقص في هدايته

IBNMAJAH:3790/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:3790/r1.speaker: النبي
IBNMAJAH:3790/r1.claim: Abu al-Darda reports the Prophet's teaching that remembrance of God is the best deed, most pleasing to God and highest in rank, better than wealth or combat.
IBNMAJAH:3790/r1.anchor: قَالُوا وَمَا ذَاكَ يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ قَالَ ‏"‏ ذِكْرُ اللَّهِ ‏"‏

IBNMAJAH:3790/r2.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:3790/r2.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
IBNMAJAH:3790/r2.claim: Muadh b. Jabal says no deed saves a person more from God's punishment than remembrance of God.
IBNMAJAH:3790/r2.anchor: وقال معاذ بن جبل ما عمل امرؤ بعمل أنجى له من عذاب الله عز وجل من ذكر الله

IBNMAJAH:3793/r1.author: IBNMAJAH
IBNMAJAH:3793/r1.speaker: رسول الله
IBNMAJAH:3793/r1.claim: A Bedouin asks the Prophet for one Islamic practice to hold fast to; he replies that the man's tongue should remain moist with remembrance of God.
IBNMAJAH:3793/r1.anchor: قَالَ لِرَسُولِ اللَّهِ ـ صلى الله عليه وسلم ـ إِنَّ شَرَائِعَ الإِسْلَامِ قَدْ كَثُرَتْ عَلَىَّ

MALIK:493/r1.author: MALIK
MALIK:493/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء
MALIK:493/r1.claim: Abu al-Darda presents remembrance of God as a deed surpassing spending gold and silver and meeting the enemy in battle.
MALIK:493/r1.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء ألا أخبركم بخير، أعمالكم وأرفعها في درجاتكم

MALIK:493/r2.author: MALIK
MALIK:493/r2.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
MALIK:493/r2.claim: Muadh ibn Jabal says no human deed is more likely to save a person from God's punishment than remembrance of God.
MALIK:493/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الرحمن معاذ بن جبل ما عمل ابن آدم من عمل أنجى له من عذاب الله من ذكر الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r1.claim: A report says this verse was revealed about Ali and Hamza as those whose hearts were opened, and Abu Lahab and his son as those whose hearts were hardened.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r1.anchor: روي أن هذه الآية: أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام آية نزلت في علي وحمزة، وأبي لهب وابنه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r2.claim: An omitted comparison is understood: Is the one whose chest God opened like the hard-hearted person who turns away from God's command?
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r2.anchor: وفي الكلام محذوف يدل الظاهر عليه، تقديره: أفمن شرح الله صدره كالقاسي القلب المعرض عن أمر الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r3.claim: Opening the chest is a metaphor for acquiring sound reflection and belief in God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r3.anchor: وشرح الصدر: استعارة لتحصيله للنظر الجيد والإيمان بالله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r4.claim: The light is God's guidance, which is much like physical light.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r4.anchor: «النور» هداية الله تعالى، وهي أشبه شيء بالضوء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet said a heart opens and expands when light enters it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن مسعود: قلنا يا رسول الله كيف انشراح الصدر؟ قال: «إذا دخل النور القلب انشرح وانفسح»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r6.claim: In the same report, the Prophet gives the sign as turning toward the eternal home, withdrawing from the deceptive home, and preparing for death before death.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r6.anchor: قالوا وما علامة ذلك؟ قال: «الإنابة إلى دار الخلود، والتجافي عن دار الغرور، والتأهب للموت قبل الموت»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r7.claim: قسوة is hardness, named from the hardness of stone; the disbeliever's heart resembles stone in its deviation and resistance to admonition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r7.anchor: مأخوذة من قسوة الحجر، شبه قلب الكافر به في ضلالته وقلة انفعاله للوعظ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r8.speaker: مالك بن دينار
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r8.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says no punishment inflicted on a servant is greater than a hardened heart.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r8.anchor: وقال مالك بن دينار: ما ضرب العبد بعقوبة أعظم من قسوة قلب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r9.claim: The phrase woe to the hard-hearted points back to the omitted comparison.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p527#2/r9.anchor: ويدل قوله: فويل للقاسية على المحذوف المقدر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the comparison's answer is omitted but understood: is the one whose chest God opened and who was guided like one whose heart was sealed and not guided?
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج جوابه متروك لأن الكلام دال عليه تقديره أفمن شرح الله صدره فاهتدى كمن طبع على قلبه فلم يهتد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r2.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet recited this verse; when asked what the opening of the chest meant, he gave a hadith Ibn al-Jawzi had cited under 6:125.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r2.anchor: وقد روى ابن مسعود أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تلا هذه الآية فقلنا يا رسول الله وما هذا الشرح فذكر حديثا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the light is certainty.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r3.anchor: ﴿ فهو على نور ﴾ فيه أربعة أقوال أحدها اليقين قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r4.claim: Qatada says the light is God's Book, which the believer follows and makes his guide.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r4.anchor: والثاني كتاب الله يأخذ به وينتهي إليه قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r5.speaker: ابن السائب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r5.claim: Ibn al-Sa'ib says the light is clarity or explanation.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r6.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r6.claim: Muqatil says the light is guidance.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r7.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn Abbas that the verse concerns Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r7.anchor: أحدها أنها نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق وأبي بن خلف رواه الضحاك عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r8.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r8.claim: Ata says the verse concerns Ali, Hamza, Abu Lahab, and Abu Lahab's son.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r8.anchor: والثاني في علي وحمزة وأبي لهب و ولده قاله عطاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r9.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r9.claim: Muqatil says the verse contrasts the Prophet with Abu Jahl.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p173/r9.anchor: والثالث في رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وفي أبي جهل قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r1.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi refers back to his explanation of hardness in al-Baqara 2:74.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r1.anchor: قد بينا معنى القساوة في البقرة 74

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r2.claim: When the remembrance they deny is recited to them, their hearts harden against believing it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r2.anchor: كلما تلي عليهم ذكر الله الذي يكذبون به قست قلوبهم عن الإيمان به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r3.claim: Mujahid and others take min here to mean ʿan, “away from” or “against.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r3.anchor: وذهب مقاتل في آخرين إلى أن من هاهنا بمعنى عن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r4.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r4.claim: Al-Farraʾ adduces Arab usage in which عن and من both follow أتخمت to mean becoming overfull from food.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r4.anchor: قال الفراء كما تقول أتخمت عن طعام أكلته ومن طعام أكلته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r5.claim: Their denial made them deem God's remembrance false, and that denial hardened their hearts.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r6.claim: Those who understand the hearts as hardening away from remembrance mean that they turned away from it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r6.anchor: ومن قال قست قلوبهم عنه أراد أعرضت عنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب وابن أبي عبلة وأبو عمران
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r7.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Ibn Abi ʿAbla, and Abu ʿImran read عن ذكر الله in place of من ذكر الله.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p174/r7.anchor: قرأ أبي بن كعب وابن أبي عبلة وأبو عمران قلوبهم عن ذكر الله مكان قوله من

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#2/r1.claim: One whose heart God opens to Islam and who walks by His light cannot be equal to someone hard-hearted and far from truth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#2/r1.anchor: أي: هل يستوي هذا ومن هو قاسي القلب بعيد من الحق

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#2/r2.claim: Hard hearts do not soften at God's remembrance, become humble, or receive and understand it; their owners are manifestly astray.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p93#2/r2.anchor: أي: فلا تلين عند ذكره (3) ، ولا تخشع ولا تعي ولا تفهم

MUSNAD-AHMAD:17680/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:17680/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن بسر
MUSNAD-AHMAD:17680/r1.claim: ʿAbd Allah ibn Busr reports that, when asked for a comprehensive practice, the Prophet advised keeping the tongue continually moist with remembrance of God, echoing the verse's concern with God's remembrance.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:17680/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن بسر، قال: أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أعرابيان

MUSNAD-AHMAD:17698/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:17698/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن بسر
MUSNAD-AHMAD:17698/r1.claim: ʿAbd Allah ibn Busr reports that, when asked for an act to hold fast to amid many Islamic duties, the Prophet advised constant remembrance of God, echoing the verse's concern with God's remembrance.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:17698/r1.anchor: سمعت عبد الله بن بسر يقول

MUSNAD-AHMAD:22079/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:22079/r1.speaker: رسول الله
MUSNAD-AHMAD:22079/r1.claim: Muʿadh reports the Prophet saying that no deed better saves a person from God's punishment than remembrance of God, directly reinforcing the verse's contrast with hearts hardened against remembrance.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:22079/r1.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ما عمل آدمي عملا قط أنجى له من عذاب الله من ذكر الله "

MUSNAD-AHMAD:22079/r2.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:22079/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:22079/r2.claim: Muʿadh reports that the Prophet calls remembrance of God the best, purest, and highest deed, superior to wealth and fighting, supporting the verse's emphasis on remembrance.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:22079/r2.anchor: وقال معاذ: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r1.claim: Sharḥ here means opening and expansion, so that the heart accepts something; the verb can also mean explaining or cutting open.
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r1.anchor: الشرح: الانفتاح والسعة، يقال: شرح صدره: إذا انفتح، واتسع بالشيء فيقبله

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r2.claim: Qaswa means misguidance; a hard heart is coarse and thick, and qasāwa is a variant form.
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r2.anchor: والقسوة: الضلالة، وكل صلب فهو قاس، ومنه: قسوة القلب: جفاؤه وغلظته

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r6.claim: One construal supplies a comparison with those whose hearts are hardened.
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r6.anchor: ويقال في قوله: (أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام) كالقاسية قلوبهم

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r7.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r7.claim: One ellipsis supplies: Is the person whose heart God opened by proofs and who became Muslim like a misguided sinner?
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r7.anchor: وقيل: محذوف، تقديره: أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام بالدلائل ومثلها، وصار مسلما كمن كان ضالا فاسقا

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r8.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r8.claim: Another supplies a comparison between the guided person whose heart was opened and the hardened person who did not find guidance.
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r8.anchor: وقيل: أفمن شرح الله صدره فاهتدى كمن قسا قلبه فلم يهتد

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r10.speaker: مقاتل
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r10.claim: Muqatil says the verse about the person whose heart is opened was revealed concerning the Prophet.
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r10.anchor: وقيل: بل نزل في رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، عن مقاتل

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r11.claim: One report says the verse about the opened heart was revealed concerning ʿAmmar ibn Yasir.
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r11.anchor: قيل: نزلي قوله: (أفمن شرح الله صدره) في عمار بن ياسر

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود، وابن عباس
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r12.claim: Ibn Masʿud and Ibn ʿAbbas identify Abu Jahl and similar unbelievers as those with hardened hearts.
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r12.anchor: (فويل للقاسية قلوبهم) أبو جهل وأمثاله من الكفار، عن ابن مسعود، وابن عباس

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r15.claim: This connects to the prior proofs of divine unity and justice: reflection on them opens the discerning person’s heart to unity.
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r15.anchor: قلنا: بما قبله من ذكر أدلة التوحيد والعدل الذي إذا تفكر فيها العاقل انشرح صدره، وسكنت نفسه إلى التوحيد

JISHUMI:v8p6053/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r16.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p6053/r16.claim: The light from the preceding verse is identified here as the Quran.

TIRMIDHI:3375/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3375/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن بسر
TIRMIDHI:3375/r1.claim: A man overwhelmed by many Islamic duties asks for a practice to hold onto; the Prophet tells him to keep his tongue moist with remembrance of God. Al-Tirmidhi grades it hasan gharib.
TIRMIDHI:3375/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن بسر، رضى الله عنه

TIRMIDHI:3377/r1.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3377/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء
TIRMIDHI:3377/r1.claim: Abu al-Darda reports the Prophet ranking remembrance of God above charity and even combat as the best and most elevating deed; Tirmidhi gives no explicit grade.
TIRMIDHI:3377/r1.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء، رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ قَالَ

TIRMIDHI:3377/r2.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3377/r2.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
TIRMIDHI:3377/r2.claim: Muadh adds that nothing better saves a person from God's punishment than remembrance of God.
TIRMIDHI:3377/r2.anchor: فقال معاذ بن جبل رضى الله عنه ما شيء أنجى من عذاب الله من ذكر الله

TIRMIDHI:3377/r3.author: TIRMIDHI
TIRMIDHI:3377/r3.speaker: author
TIRMIDHI:3377/r3.claim: Al-Tirmidhi notes that some narrators preserve this connected chain, while others transmit it mursal from Abdullah ibn Sa'id; he gives no explicit grade.
TIRMIDHI:3377/r3.anchor: قال أبو عيسى وقد روى بعضهم هذا الحديث عن عبد الله بن سعيد مثل هذا بهذا الإسناد وروى بعضهم عنه فأرسله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r1.claim: God knows who is fit for لطف and grants it, so that the person’s breast opens to Islam, welcomes it, and accepts it; one without this لطف remains constricted and hard-hearted.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r1.anchor: عرف الله أنه من أهل اللطف فلطف به حتى انشرح صدره للإسرم ورغب فيه وقبله كمن لا لطف له فهو حرج الصدر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r2.claim: The light from his Lord is God’s لطف.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r3.claim: After reciting the verse, the Prophet says the heart opens and expands when light enters it; its sign is turning toward the eternal home, leaving worldly delusion, and preparing for death.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r3.anchor: وقرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r4.claim: The rhetorical question omits its predicate, as does the construction in 39:9.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r4.anchor: في حذف الخبر { من ذكر الله } من أجل ذكره

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r5.claim: Here من means because of remembrance: when God or His signs are mentioned to the hard-hearted, they recoil and grow still more hardened, like those addressed in 9:125.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r5.anchor: من أجل ذكره ، أي : إذا ذكر الله عندهم أو آياته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r6.claim: A variant reads عن ذكر الله.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r6.anchor: وقرىء : ( عن ذكر الله ) فإن قلت : ما الفرق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r7.claim: With من, hardness arises because of remembrance; with عن, the heart is too hardened and estranged to accept remembrance. He illustrates the contrast with giving water because of thirst versus giving it until thirst is gone.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p124/r7.anchor: قسا قلبه من ذكر الله ، فالمعنى ما ذكرت

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi say God widened his breast so Islam would be established in it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r1.anchor: أحدهما : وسع صدره للإسلام حتى يثبت فيه , قاله ابن عباس والسدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r2.claim: Alternatively, Islam brings joy and tranquility; this expansion cannot precede Islam, unlike the first view.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r2.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون الشرح قبل الإسلام

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r3.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r3.claim: Al-Suddi interprets the light as God's guidance.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r3.anchor: أحدهما : على هدى من ربه , قاله السدي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r4.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r4.claim: Qatada interprets it as God's Book, which is followed and returned to.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r4.anchor: الثاني : أنه كتاب الله الذي به يأخذ وإليه ينتهي , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r5.claim: The Prophet says expansion is a light cast in the heart, marked by turning to eternity, renouncing delusion, and preparing for death before death.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r5.anchor: تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية , فقالوا : يا رسول الله ما هذا الشرح ؟

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r6.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r6.claim: Al-Kalbi says the verse was revealed about the Prophet.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r6.anchor: أحدها : في رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم , قاله الكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r7.speaker: النقاش
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r7.claim: Al-Naqqash reports it was revealed about Umar.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r7.anchor: الثاني : في عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه , حكاه النقاش

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r8.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r8.claim: Muqatil says it was revealed about Ammar ibn Yasir.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r8.anchor: الثالث : في عمار بن ياسر , قاله مقاتل

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r9.claim: The hard-hearted are Abu Jahl and Quraysh's unbelievers.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r9.anchor: قيل أنه عنى أبا جهل وأتباعه من كفار قريش

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r10.claim: An omitted comparison means the person on light is unlike one whose heart God sealed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p121/r10.anchor: فهو على نور من ربه كمن طبع الله على قلبه

MUQATIL:39:21-23/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:21-23/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:21-23/r4.claim: God's opening of the chest means widening the heart for monotheism; the one on his Lord's light is Muhammad, on guidance.
MUQATIL:39:21-23/r4.anchor: يقول: أفمن وسع الله قلبه للتوحيد { فهو على نور } يعنى على هدى { من ربه } يعنى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

MUQATIL:39:21-23/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:21-23/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:21-23/r5.claim: The hard-hearted person is Abū Jahl, whose heart did not soften.
MUQATIL:39:21-23/r5.anchor: { فويل للقاسية } يعنى الجافية { قلوبهم } فلم تلن، يعنى أبا جهل

MUQATIL:39:21-23/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:39:21-23/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:39:21-23/r6.claim: Here being hardened from God's remembrance means being turned away from God's oneness; the two people are not alike.
MUQATIL:39:21-23/r6.anchor: يعنى عن توحيد الله { أولئك فى ضلال مبين } [آية: 22] يعنى أبا جهل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r1.claim: God expanded the person's heart for Islam, enabling guidance.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r1.anchor: ﴿ أفمن شرح الله صدره ﴾ أى وسع صدره

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r2.speaker: محمد ﷺ
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r2.claim: The Prophet said light entering a heart expands it; its sign is longing for the eternal home, turning from delusion, and preparing for death before it arrives.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r2.anchor: وسئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الشرح فقال إذا دخل النور القلب انشرح وانفسح فقيل فهل لذلك من علامة قال نعم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r3.claim: Being on light from one's Lord means having clarity and insight.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r3.anchor: ﴿ فهو على نور من ربه ﴾ بيان وبصيرة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r4.claim: The comparison asks whether the guided person is like one whose heart is sealed and hardened; it is omitted because the following warning implies it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r4.anchor: المعنى أفمن شرح الله صدره فاهتدى كمن طبع على قلبه فقسا قلبه فحذف

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r5.claim: من may mean their hearts harden from abandoning God's remembrance, or because remembrance and His signs make them harder, as in the verse about added defilement.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r5.anchor: من ترك ذكر الله أو من أجل ذكر الله أى إذا ذكر الله عندهم أو آياته ازدادت قلوبهم قساوة كقوله فزادتهم رجسا إلى رجسهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r6.claim: Those people are in manifest error.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p52/r6.anchor: ﴿ أولئك في ضلال مبين ﴾ غواية ظاهرة

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r1.claim: Sharḥ means opening and making spacious.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says God widened the person’s breast to Islam until it became firm within him.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وسع صدره للإسلام حتى ثبت فيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r3.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says Islam expanded the breast through joy and tranquility; on this reading, the expansion follows Islam, whereas Ibn Abbas’s reading allows it to precede it.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r3.anchor: وقال السدي: وسع صدره بالإسلام للفرح به والطمأنينة إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r4.claim: Being on light means being guided by God, in contrast with one whose heart is sealed and hardened.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r4.anchor: أي على هدى من ربه كمن طبع على قلبه وأقساه

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r5.speaker: المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad says qasā means becoming hard; ʿatā and ʿasā are close in meaning, and a hard heart does not soften.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r5.anchor: قال المبرد: يقال قسا القلب إذا صلب، وكذلك عتا وعسا مقاربة لها.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r6.speaker: المفسرون
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r6.claim: The commentators identify the person whose breast was expanded as ʿAli and Hamza.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r6.anchor: والمراد بمن شرح الله صدره هاهنا فيما ذكر المفسرون علي وحمزة

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r7.speaker: النقاش
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r7.claim: Al-Naqqash reports that the referent is Umar ibn al-Khattab.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r7.anchor: وحكى النقاش أنه عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r8.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r8.claim: Muqatil identifies the referent as ʿAmmar ibn Yasir.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r9.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r9.claim: Muqatil also reports, together with al-Kalbi, that the referent is the Messenger of God.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r9.anchor: وعنه أيضا والكلبي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r10.claim: The verse applies generally to anyone in whose heart God creates faith and thereby expands the breast.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r10.anchor: والآية عامة فيمن شرح الله صدره بخلق الإيمان فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r11.claim: In a report from Ibn Masud, the Prophet says light entering the heart opens it; its signs are turning to the eternal home, detaching from delusion, and preparing for death before it arrives.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r11.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: قلنا يا رسول الله قوله تعالى: { أفمن شرح الله صدره

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r12.claim: A report in al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim’s Nawadir al-Usul from Ibn Umar calls the wisest believer one who remembers death most and prepares best; it repeats that light opens the heart and lists the same three signs.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r12.anchor: وخرجه الترمذي الحكيم في «نوادر الأصول» من حديث ابن عمر:

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r13.claim: The three signs mark complete faith: inabah consists of good works because the eternal home is their reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r13.anchor: فذكر صلى الله عليه وسلم خصالا ثلاث، ولا شك أن من كانت فيه هذه الخصال فهو الكامل الإيمان

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r14.claim: Paradise is the reward for deeds, as God says in the verse cited here.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22/r14.anchor: ألا ترى كيف ذكره الله في مواضع في تنزيله

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r1.claim: A servant turns toward the eternal home by persisting in good works; detachment means curbing worldly desire, accepting what suffices, and being content.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r1.anchor: فإذا انكمش العبد في أعمال البر فهو إنابته إلى دار الخلود

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r2.claim: Readiness for death means acting with taqwa, deliberation, caution, and scrupulous avoidance of doubtful matters; these are outward signs.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r2.anchor: وإذا أحكم أموره بالتقوى فكان ناظرا في كل أمر، واقفا متأدبا متثبتا حذرا

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r3.claim: These signs arise from seeing death and the afterlife as displacing the deceptive world; that vision comes through light entering the heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r3.anchor: وإنما صار هكذا لرؤية الموت، ورؤية صرف الآخرة عن الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r4.claim: One view takes the hard-hearted as Abu Lahab and his children.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r5.claim: On one reading, hearing God’s remembrance makes their hearts even harder.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r5.anchor: ومعنى: «من ذكر الله» أن قلوبهم تزداد قسوة

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r6.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r6.claim: Al-Tabari takes min to mean ʿan: their hearts hardened against accepting God’s remembrance.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: إن «من» بمعنى عن، والمعنى قست عن قبول ذكر الله. وهذا اختيار الطبري.

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r7.speaker: الله تعالى
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r7.claim: In a report from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, God says to seek needs from generous people, who contain His mercy, rather than hard-hearted people, who contain His anger.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r7.anchor: قال الله تعالى اطلبوا الحوائج من السمحاء فإني جعلت فيهم رحمتي

QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r8.speaker: مالك بن دينار
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r8.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says no punishment is greater than a hardened heart, and that God removes mercy from a people when angry with them.
QURTUBI-FULL:39:22#2/r8.anchor: وقال مالك بن دينار: ما ضرب عبد بعقوبة أعظم من قسوة قلب
